subject: Answers + proposed exception path for uptime/latency questionnaire
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-enterprises.com>

Cc: procurement@acme-enterprises.com
Date: 2026-11-27T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Procurement questionnaire: uptime/latency measurement + exception request

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement team has a short questionnaire focused on how Redwood measures uptime and latency, and what an exception path looks like for workloads that routinely hit high tail latency (we run nightly bulk inference jobs). The questionnaire is attached. Key asks:

- How do you define "uptime" (calculation window, excluded maintenance windows)?
- How is P99 latency computed (end-to-end, sampling, inclusion/exclusion of cold starts)?
- What monitoring and alerting thresholds does Redwood provide to customers?
- Can customers access raw/aggregated metrics dashboards and for what retention window?
- Process for an "SLO exception" (approval timeline, mitigation, credits, controls)?

We'd like answers by end of day Monday so procurement can finish their review. Also, we are formally requesting an exception path for our nightly bulk runs that cause regular P99 spikes — we'd prefer a controlled exemption vs. a blanket SLA waiver.

Attached: acme_slo_questionnaire.pdf

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Enterprises

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: uptime/latency measurement + exception request

Sarah — thanks for the questionnaire and context. High level answers below and I attached a 7-day sample metrics export and a Grafana view link for transparency. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to walk the details.

Short answers (details below):
- Uptime: measured as "serving availability" per customer over a rolling 30-day window; planned maintenance windows are excluded when pre-notified per contract.
- P99 latency: computed end-to-end at the request boundary; we use server-side instrumentation and exclude cold-starts for dedicated/private deployments (we mark warmup period for autoscaling events).
- Monitoring/alerts: default alerts for availability drop >0.5% on a 1h window and P99 degradation >250ms over baseline; custom alerting and per-route thresholds available via Console.
- Customer access: Grafana dashboards and a dedicated metrics export (retention 90 days for hosted customers, longer for Dedicated/Private under agreement).
- Exception path: we support conditional SLO exceptions — requires a documented plan, capacity controls, and an agreed credit/mitigation plan; typical approval 3–7 business days.

Attached: sample-metrics-7day.csv
Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/uptime-latency-acme

I'll loop in Lauren for the detailed measurement definitions and Priyom for contractual/compliance items.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-enterprises.com>

Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: uptime/latency measurement + exception request

Adding technical specifics to Diego's notes — written for the questionnaire answers.

Uptime (serving availability):
- Definition: percentage of successful inference requests over total non-errored requests per rolling 30-day window. Successful = 2xx or business-meaningful structured response (no retry required).
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (>=48h notice), customer-managed network outages (for Private/VPC), and documented migration windows.
- Calculation samples: we compute per-route and aggregated account-level availability; exported as daily windows and computed again for rolling windows.

P99 latency:
- Definition: 99th percentile of end-to-end request latency measured at the ingress edge where request completes and response is handed back to the customer (includes queuing + model time).
- Sampling & cold starts: for Hosted we log cold starts and annotate metrics; default P99 excludes first N requests after an autoscale or deployment event (warmup window configurable). For Dedicated/Private, cold-starts are typically absent or separately flagged.

Monitoring & Alerts:
- Out-of-the-box rules:
  * Availability alert: triggered when 30-day rolling availability drops below contracted SLO by >0.5% sustained for 1h.
  * Latency alert: triggered when P99 exceeds baseline + threshold (baseline set at contract time).
- Escalation: PagerDuty integration available; alert details include recent traces and a time-sliced metric export.

Customer access & retention:
- Dashboards: read-only Grafana links per account (90 days retention by default for hosted).
- Exports: CSV/JSON exports for requested windows; raw traces retained 30 days; aggregated metrics 90 days. Longer retention offered in Dedicated/Private contracts.

Exception path (operational controls):
- Trigger: customer files an exception request describing the workload, expected cadence, and mitigation controls.
- Review: SRE + Solutions review (2–3 business days), procurement & legal review for credit/contract terms (3–7 business days).
- Conditions: exception approved with one or more of: capped throughput for the bulk window, routing to dedicated pool, temporary quota increase, or separate billing for burst runs.
- Reciprocity: we require monitoring hooks and a rollback plan; we also offer an "exception label" that excludes identified windows from SLA calculations.

I'll join any call to walk the metrics definitions.

— Lauren
Principal Product Manager, Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai

Procurement/compliance items from my side to support approval:

1) Evidence: please confirm log retention (we retain request logs for 30 days by default; aggregated metric rollups 90 days). If Acme needs longer retention for audit we can add to contract.
2) Controls: for approved exceptions we require a documented runbook and a scheduled window; Redwood will not count exception windows toward availability SLO if the run is labeled and meets the rollback/monitoring criteria.
3) Credits & billing: exceptions are not automatic credits — if an exception results in reduced SLA exposure we will document the absence of credits; if the exception increases risk to availability we will negotiate a credit schedule.
4) Docs/Signoff: I can prepare a short Exception Addendum to be appended to the MSA; will include: start/end dates, labeling rules, monitoring hook, and termination terms.

Action: Diego — can you confirm whether Acme wants a recurring scheduled exception (e.g., nightly 02:00–04:00 PST) or ad-hoc runs? Also Sarah — please confirm retention needs. If you approve, I'll draft the addendum and share a DocuSign link.

— Priyom
Head of Contracts & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our sync:

- Acme confirmed the nightly bulk runs are scheduled 02:00–03:30 PST and are expected to continue as recurring.
- We will label those windows as "acme:bulk-nightly" in telemetry so they are excluded from SLA calculations once the Exception Addendum is signed.
- Redwood proposes: temporary dedicated burst capacity during the window (meters usage), monitoring hooks with PagerDuty alerts to Acme ops, and 90-day metric retention (extendable if you need).

I attached the initial Exception Addendum draft (agreed-exception-statement.pdf) and the sample metrics we discussed. Priyom will send the DocuSign link after you confirm retention and that the scheduled window is correct.

Next steps:
1) Sarah: confirm retention (90 days OK?) and that the 02:00–03:30 PST window is accurate.
2) Priyom: draft and circulate DocuSign addendum.
3) Lauren: we'll schedule a 30-min technical runbook review with Acme ops.

Thanks — happy to take this to signature this week.

Best,
